title: The Potential of Aloe vera and Opuntia ficus-indica Extracts as Biobased Agents for Cultural Heritage Metal Conservation
content: Metal conservators face challenges in restoring archaeologically significant metal items, particularly copper and its alloys, due to biocorrosion from bacteria. Research focuses on effective, eco-friendly methods for removing microbiological corrosion and preserving cultural heritage. We assessed the antibacterial and antibiofilm properties of Aloe vera and Opuntia ficus-indica extracts, which have unique secondary metabolites. These plants have already been investigated as corrosion inhibitors, but not as biocorrosion inhibitors for metals against a specific type of corrosive bacteria, Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Time-kill assays were conducted to evaluate antimicrobial activity. Both plant extracts exhibited strong antimicrobial activity, eliminating nearly all bacterial strains in every test. We evaluated the anti-biofilm efficiency on copper, brass, and bronze using the spread-plate method and microscopic staining. The extracts left removable traces on the metal surfaces, essential for future conservation and restoration use.
